name: Leang Karampuang painted figurative scene
description: A Sulawesi cave panel places human-like figures alongside a pig, preserving an early example of representational scene-making.

impact.note: One cave panel witnessing early scene-making; no later work is known to descend from this painting.

date.label: At least 51,200 years ago
date.basis: Carbonate over one human-like figure yields a conservative minimum 51.2 ka; for calendar indexing the older-than bound is conservatively rounded to 49,000 BCE.

events.statement: A panel at Leang Karampuang depicts a pig and at least three associated human-like figures.
events.scope: The minimum date concerns overlying carbonate, not pigment directly; the proposed single composition and depicted actions are interpretations. The story and makers are unknown. Only one human-like figure is directly bounded by the sampled carbonate; assigning the age to the entire scene depends on the interpretation that its figures form one composition.
events.caveats: The minimum date concerns overlying carbonate, not pigment directly; the proposed single composition and depicted actions are interpretations. The story and makers are unknown. Only one human-like figure is directly bounded by the sampled carbonate; assigning the age to the entire scene depends on the interpretation that its figures form one composition.
